title: Bezalel the craftsman
hook: Bezalel is filled with spirit to work in gold, stone and wood (Exodus 31:1–5)

segments.voice: Yesterday, six days, then a stop that includes everyone within the gates. Your line was six days, then stop. Did you find your edge? Day eight hundred eighty-three.

The plans are already given: curtains, a chest, a lampstand, a tent of worship, all of it to be made by hand, out in the wilderness. In the book of Exodus, Moses has been shown the design. What they need now is someone who can do the work. A jeweler's eye. A stonemason's straight line. A carpenter's palm that feels what the eye misses. God calls a craftsman by name. Today: Bezalel the craftsman.
screen: `THE PLANS ARE GIVEN.` → `A TENT TO BE MADE BY HAND.` → `A CRAFTSMAN, CALLED BY NAME.`

segments.voice: First, the call. “See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.” The King James spells it Bezaleel. He's named with his father, his father's father and his tribe. In this story, the one who works with his hands is not anonymous labor. He's called, personally, by name. Second, the gift. “And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship.” Then the text lists what the spirit is for: to work in gold and silver and brass, to cut and set stones, to carve timber. Here the spirit of God doesn't arrive as a vision or a voice. It arrives in the hands. Wisdom, in this chapter, includes knowing how to set a stone straight. Third, the teaching. A few chapters on, the text says he was given it in his heart to teach, he and a partner named Aholiab. The skill isn't a secret to hoard. It's handed on, from one pair of hands to the next. Fourth, the edge from yesterday. Right after Bezalel is named, the same chapter turns back to the sabbath: “Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep.” Some readers, the medieval commentator Rashi among them, take the order as a lesson: even the work of building a holy place stops on the seventh day. So craft, in Exodus, is holy, and it still rests. A careful weld, a well-cut sleeve, a cake with straight layers: a reader of this chapter could call any of them a gift of the spirit.
screen: `CALLED BY NAME.` · `FILLED WITH SPIRIT, FOR CRAFT.` · `GIVEN THE HEART TO TEACH.` · `EVEN HOLY WORK STOPS.` · then, large: `CRAFT IS HOLY.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and rest your hands in your lap or on a table. Feel them. The fingertips. The palms. The small muscles you only notice when they're tired. These hands have made things: a meal, a bed, a note, a repair. Now bring to mind one thing you could make today, small and real. A sandwich made with care. A drawing. A sewn-on button. A loaf, a shelf, a card. Picture the very first motion your hands would make. Hold it. After the bell, you can make it, slowly, as if it mattered. If you pray, you can hold that making in your own tradition's words. The bell holds the time.
Bezalel the craftsman. From Exodus: the maker called by name and filled with the spirit of God to work in gold, stone and wood. Today's word.
Your line: craft is holy. Today, make one thing with your hands, and give it your full attention while you make it. Day eight hundred eighty-three.

howItsDone: Some Jewish and Christian readers point to Bezalel when they speak of craft and art as a gift of the spirit.

notes: The original-language card gives the Hebrew spelling בְּצַלְאֵל; confirm pointing. No meaning of the name is claimed.
The hook's list (curtains, a chest, a lampstand) paraphrases Exodus 25–27.
'Given it in his heart to teach' paraphrases Exodus 35:34 (KJV: 'he hath put in his heart that he may teach').
Editor: hook reopened on the plans rather than a list of workers (879 and 886 also open on image lists); practice no longer repeats the open-hands posture of 867 and 876.

Auditor: hook corrected (the pattern is shown to Moses, Exodus 25:9, not 'the people'); 'even holy work stops' is an inference from the juxtaposition, now attributed to readers such as Rashi on Exodus 31:13. Confirm with a Judaism Keeper.
